p.src: Now, when Lady Qin heard Baoyu call out her childhood name in his dream, she was naturally puzzled, but could hardly question him closely. At that moment Baoyu was dazed and bewildered, as though he had lost something. The attendants hurriedly brought him longan soup; after sipping twice, he rose and straightened his clothes. When Xiren reached out to fasten his trouser sash, her hand happened to brush his thigh, where she felt a cold, wet patch; startled, she snatched her hand away and asked what had happened. Baoyu flushed crimson and gave her hand a squeeze. Xiren was an intelligent girl, two years older than Baoyu, and had lately begun to understand the ways of men and women. Seeing Baoyu in such a state, she guessed half the truth; her face too turned crimson with shame, and she dared ask no more. She finished arranging his clothes as before, and they went to Grandmother Jia's apartments. After hastily eating supper there, they returned to this side of the compound.

p.src: Taking advantage of a moment when the nurses and maids were not nearby, Xiren hurriedly fetched another pair of under-trousers and changed Baoyu into them. Baoyu pleaded bashfully, “Dear sister, whatever you do, don't tell anyone.” Xiren, also blushing, asked with a smile, “What did you dream about? Where did all that filthy stuff come from?” “It's a long story,” Baoyu replied. Thereupon he related to Xiren in detail everything that had happened in his dream. When he came to the art of cloud and rain taught him by Disenchantment, Xiren was so embarrassed that she covered her face, bent over, and laughed. Baoyu had always been fond of Xiren's gentle charm and pretty ways, and now he pressed her to join him in practising what Disenchantment had taught him about cloud and rain. Xiren had long known that Grandmother Jia had given her to Baoyu, so she did not consider this a breach of propriety. She therefore secretly tried it with him, and fortunately no one came upon them. From that time on, Baoyu regarded Xiren as more special than any of the others, while Xiren devoted herself to him more wholeheartedly than ever. For the present, there is nothing more to tell of this.

p.src: Now, counting all the people in the Rong household together, their number was not enormous, yet from the highest to the lowest there were still three or four hundred souls. Though its affairs were not many, some ten or twenty arose each day, all tangled like a skein of hemp, with no single thread that might serve as a guiding line. Just as I was pondering which affair and which person would best begin the tale, there happened to come from a thousand leagues away a tiny household, insignificant as a mustard seed or bean, which had some slight connection with the Rong household and was that very day making its way there. To begin with this family, then, provides a thread after all. What, you ask, was this family's name, and what connection did it have with the Rong household? If, worthy readers, you find such details trivial and vulgar, quickly cast this book aside and seek some finer work to refresh your eyes; but if you think it may serve to dispel an idle hour, allow this foolish creature to relate the particulars. The humble family just mentioned were natives of the district and bore the surname Wang. One of their ancestors had once held a minor post in the capital and had known in former years the father of Lady Wang, who was also Grandmother Wang to Xifeng. Coveting the Wang family's power and influence, he claimed kinship with them and was acknowledged as a nephew. At that time only Lady Wang's eldest brother—Xifeng's father—and Lady Wang herself were living in the capital and knew of this affiliated branch of the clan; none of the others knew them. By now that ancestor was dead. He had left only one son, Wang Cheng, who, as the family fortunes declined, moved back out of the city to their native village. Wang Cheng too had recently died of illness, leaving only his son, whose childhood name was Gou'er. Gou'er had a son of his own, nicknamed Ban'er; his lawful wife, née Liu, had also borne him a daughter named Qing'er. The family of four still made their living by farming. Since Gou'er went out by day to earn a little extra, while his wife drew water, pounded grain, and attended to the other household tasks, there was no one to look after Qing'er and Ban'er. Gou'er therefore brought his mother-in-law, Grannie Liu, to live with them. Grannie Liu was an elderly widow of many years, with neither son nor daughter of her own, and lived solely on the yield of two meagre mu of land. Naturally she was delighted when her son-in-law invited her to live under his roof, and from then on she devoted herself to helping her daughter and son-in-law make a living. That year, as autumn ended and winter began, the weather was turning cold, yet the household had made none of its winter preparations. Gou'er could not help worrying. After drinking a few cups to drown his cares, he picked quarrels at home for no reason, while his wife dared not answer back. Grannie Liu could no longer bear to watch and advised him, “Son-in-law, don't be angry with me for speaking out of turn. We country folk must all live honestly, eating according to the size of the bowl we possess. When you were young, thanks to the good fortune of your old family, you grew accustomed to eating and drinking well; that is why you cannot manage yourself now. When you have money, you spend without thought for what comes after; when you have none, you fly into a blind rage. What sort of manly fellow behaves like that? Though we live outside the city now, we are still at the Son of Heaven's feet.

p.src: The streets of Chang'an are strewn with money; the only pity is that no one knows how to pick it up. Stamping and fretting at home will do no good.” At this Gou'er retorted irritably, “All you can do, old lady, is talk nonsense from the kang. Do you mean I should rob and steal?” “Who told you to steal?” said Grannie Liu. Still, we must all put our heads together and think of some plan. Otherwise, do you expect silver and cash to come running into our house by themselves?” Gou'er sneered. “If there were a way, would I have waited until now? I have no relatives who collect taxes and no friends in official posts. What possible plan could I devise? Even if I did, I'm afraid they would hardly pay any attention to the likes of us!”

p.src: Granny Liu said, “That is not so. Man proposes, but Heaven disposes. If we do what we can and the Bodhisattva blesses us, some opportunity may yet arise. As it happens, I have thought of an opportunity for you. Your family once claimed kinship with the Wang family of Jinling, and twenty years ago they treated you quite well. It must be because you have since put on airs and refused to cultivate the connection that you have grown apart. I remember that my daughter and I once visited them. Their second young lady was truly openhearted and straightforward, knew how to treat people, and never put on airs. She is now the wife of Second Master Jia of the Rongguo Mansion. I hear that as she has grown older, she has become more compassionate toward the poor and elderly, and especially delights in feeding monks, honoring Taoist priests, and giving away rice and money. Although the Wang family has now been transferred to a frontier post, this second aunt of yours may still remember us. Why not pay her a visit? She may remember old times and grant you some favor. If she shows even the least kindness, one hair plucked from her body would be thicker than our waists.” From the side, Madam Liu interjected, “What you say is true, Mother, but how could people with an appearance like ours present themselves at their gate? To begin with, their gatekeepers might not even agree to announce us. We would only be inviting a rebuff and public humiliation.”

p.src: Now Gou’er cared greatly for profit and advancement, so when he heard this, his interest was immediately stirred. Then, hearing his wife’s objection, he replied with a smile, “Since Granny has suggested it, and since you once met this aunt yourself, why not go there tomorrow and first see how matters stand?” Granny Liu exclaimed, “Oh, gracious me! As the saying goes, ‘The gates of the nobility are deep as the sea.’ What sort of person am I? No one in that household knows me, so I would only go there in vain.” Gou’er said with a smile, “Never mind. I shall teach you a way: take your grandson Ban’er with you and first seek out Zhou Rui, the attendant who accompanied his mistress at marriage. If you manage to see him, there may be some hope. Zhou Rui once had some dealings with my father, and our families were extremely close.” Granny Liu said, “I know him too. It has merely been so long since we had any contact that I do not know how he fares now. Well, there is no help for it. You are a man and, looking as you do, naturally cannot go. Our daughter is a young married woman and cannot well show herself about in public. So I shall have to risk this old face of mine and try my luck. If some benefit truly comes of it, we shall all profit; and even if I bring back no silver, I shall at least have seen the splendor of a ducal and noble mansion, so my life will not have been entirely in vain.” At this, they all laughed for a while. That evening, the plan was settled.

p.src: Before dawn the next day, Granny Liu rose, washed, and dressed, then gave Ban’er a few words of instruction. Ban’er was only five or six and understood nothing of the matter. Hearing that Granny Liu was taking him into the city for an outing, he was delighted and readily promised to do everything she said. Granny Liu then took him into the city and made her way to Ning-Rong Street. When they reached the stone lions before the main gate of the Rong Mansion, she saw clusters of sedan chairs and horses. Not daring to approach, Granny Liu first dusted off her clothes and again instructed Ban’er in a few things; only then did she edge toward a side gate. There she saw several men, chests thrust out and bellies bulging, sitting on a long bench, gesticulating grandly as they chatted about everything under the sun. Granny Liu had no choice but to edge forward and greet them: “May good fortune attend you, gentlemen.” The men looked her over for a while before asking, “Where have you come from?” Granny Liu answered with an ingratiating smile, “I am looking for Master Zhou, the attendant who accompanied the mistress at marriage. Might one of you gentlemen kindly ask the venerable master to come out?” They paid her no attention. Only after a long while did they say, “Go and wait over there by the corner of the wall. Someone from his household will come out presently.” One elderly man among them said, “Do not delay her business. Why make sport of her?” Then he turned to Granny Liu and said, “Master Zhou has gone south. He lives in the rear quarter, and his wife is at home. If you want to find him, go around from here to the rear street and ask at the back gate.”

p.src: Granny Liu thanked him and, taking Ban’er with her, went around to the back gate. She saw several vendors’ stands resting before the gate, some selling food and others playthings, while twenty or thirty children romped noisily about. Granny Liu caught hold of one child and asked, “Young master, may I ask whether a Madam Zhou is at home?” The children asked, “Which Madam Zhou? We have three Madam Zhous here, as well as two Mistress Zhous. What sort of work does the one you want do?” Granny Liu replied, “I mean Zhou Rui, the attendant who accompanied the mistress at marriage.” A child said, “That is easy. Follow me.” With that, he bounded ahead, leading Granny Liu through the back gate to the wall of a courtyard, where he pointed and said, “That is their home.” Then he called out, “Madam Zhou, an old granny has come to see you! I have brought her here.”

p.src: Hearing this from inside, Zhou Rui’s wife hurried out to meet them and asked, “Who is it?” Granny Liu hastened forward and greeted her: “How have you been, Sister Zhou?” Zhou Rui’s wife studied her for some time before smiling and saying, “Granny Liu, how have you been? Just think, it has only been a few years, yet I had forgotten you. Come inside and sit down.” As Granny Liu followed her inside, she said with a smile, “A person of consequence like you has so many matters to remember—how could you still remember the likes of us?” While speaking, they entered the room. Zhou Rui’s wife ordered a hired young maid to pour tea for them. Then she said to Ban’er, “You have grown so big!” She also asked about various matters since they had last met. Then she asked Granny Liu, “Are you merely passing by today, or have you come especially to see us?” Granny Liu replied, “I came especially to see you, Sister Zhou, and secondly to pay my respects to the aunt. It would be best if you could take me to see her; but if that is not possible, I must trouble you to convey my regards.”

p.src: When Zhou Rui’s wife heard this, she had already guessed something of the purpose of their visit. Years before, when her husband Zhou Rui had been embroiled in a dispute over the purchase of some land, Gou’er had done much to help him. Now that Granny Liu had come to her in this way, she found it difficult to refuse the old woman; besides, she wanted to show off her own standing in the household. At these words she smiled and said, “Don’t worry, Granny. Since you have come all this long way in perfect sincerity, surely we cannot let you go without seeing the true Buddha. Strictly speaking, receiving visitors and reporting their business has nothing to do with me. Here each of us has a separate duty: my husband attends only to collecting the rents in spring and autumn and, when he is free, escorts the young masters on their outings; I attend only to matters concerning the ladies’ excursions. But since you are a relative of Her Ladyship’s and have thought enough of me to seek my help, I shall make an exception and send word for you. There is only one thing you do not know, Granny: matters here are no longer as they were five years ago. Her Ladyship now takes little part in household affairs; Second Mistress Lian manages everything. And who do you suppose Second Mistress Lian is? She is Her Ladyship’s niece, the daughter of the elder uncle, whom we used to call little Feng.” Granny Liu was astonished. “So it is she! No wonder! I said even then that she was remarkable. In that case, I shall have to see her today as well.” “Of course,” said Zhou Rui’s wife. Her Ladyship now has so many affairs to trouble her that whenever a visitor can reasonably be excused, she declines to see them, and Miss Feng receives and entertains them all. Even if you do not see Her Ladyship today, you must see Miss Feng; otherwise your journey here will have been wasted.” “Amitabha!” exclaimed Granny Liu. “I depend entirely upon your kindness, good sister.” “You needn’t say such things,” replied Zhou Rui’s wife. As the saying goes, ‘Make things easy for others, and things will be easy for you.’ All it costs me is a word; what harm can that do me?” Then she sent a young maid to the rear hall to inquire discreetly whether the meal had yet been served in the Old Lady’s apartments. The young maid went off. Meanwhile, the two women chatted about other matters.

p.src: Granny Liu remarked, “Miss Feng cannot be more than twenty this year, yet she is capable enough to manage a household like this. That is truly remarkable.” Zhou Rui’s wife replied, “Oh, Granny, you have no idea! Young though Miss Feng is, her way of handling affairs surpasses that of anyone in the world. She has grown into a beauty, and she possesses, at the very least, ten thousand schemes within her mind. And when it comes to a battle of words, even ten eloquent men together could not outtalk her. You will believe me once you have seen her. There is only one fault: she is rather too severe with the servants.” As she spoke, the young maid returned and reported, “The Old Lady’s meal is over, and Second Mistress is in Her Ladyship’s apartments.” Hearing this, Zhou Rui’s wife sprang up and urged Granny Liu, “Quickly, quickly! When she comes down to eat, there will be a free moment; let us hurry over first. If we are one step late, there will be many others waiting to report their business, and it will be difficult to speak to her. u.src: Granny Liu remarked, “Miss Feng cannot be more than twenty this year, yet she is capable enough to manage a household like this. That is truly remarkable.”

p.src: Granny Liu heard a steady clack-clacking sound, very much like flour being sifted through a sieve in a milling chest, and could not help looking this way and that. Presently she noticed a box hanging on a pillar in the main room, with something like a scale weight suspended beneath it and swinging ceaselessly to and fro. Granny Liu wondered, “What sort of precious contraption is that? What is it used for?” While she stared blankly, there came a sudden clang, like a golden bell or bronze chime, startling her so that her eyes flew wide open. It was followed by eight or nine more strokes in succession. Just as she was about to ask what it was, all the young maids suddenly began running about in confusion, crying, “Mistress is coming down!” Zhou Rui’s wife and Ping’er hurriedly rose and told Granny Liu, “Just wait here. We shall come for you when the time is right.” With that, they both went out to welcome her.

p.src: Granny Liu held her breath, cocked her ear, and waited in silence. From far away came the sound of laughter; perhaps a dozen or twenty women, their skirts rustling, gradually entered the main room and passed into the chamber on the other side. Then she saw another two or three women come in this direction, each carrying a large lacquered serving box, and wait there. She heard someone on the other side call, “Serve the meal,” whereupon the people gradually withdrew, leaving only a few attendants to carry in the dishes. After a long spell of utter silence, two people suddenly appeared carrying a low kang table. They set it upon the kang here, its surface crowded with bowls and plates still heaped with fish and meat, though a few dishes had been sampled. The moment Ban'er saw it, he clamored for meat, and Granny Liu slapped him away. Just then, Zhou Rui's wife came over smiling and beckoned to Granny Liu. Granny Liu understood. Taking Ban'er down from the kang, she went into the main room, where Zhou Rui's wife whispered with her for a while before finally leading her into the chamber on this side.

p.src: Outside the doorway, a large scarlet curtain patterned with scattered flowers hung from chased brass hooks. Beneath the south window stood a kang covered with a long red felt mat. Against the partition on its eastern side were a brocade backrest with a linked pattern and a bolster, before them a large cushion of shimmering green satin with a golden center; beside it stood a carved-lacquer spittoon. Xifeng was dressed informally in a sable Zhaojun hood of autumn-board style, with a pearl-studded headband about it, a peach-pink flower-patterned jacket, a slate-blue tapestry-weave cape lined with grey squirrel, and a scarlet foreign-crêpe skirt lined with silver squirrel. Radiant with powder and rouge, she sat there perfectly composed, stirring the ashes in her hand-warmer with a small pair of brass tongs. Ping'er stood beside the edge of the kang, holding a small inlaid-lacquer tea tray with a little covered cup upon it. Xifeng neither took the tea nor raised her head, but went on stirring the ashes in the hand-warmer as she asked slowly, “Why haven't you invited her in yet?” As she spoke, she raised herself to take the tea and saw that Zhou Rui's wife had already brought the two visitors in and that they stood on the floor before her. Only then did she hastily make as if to rise; before she had actually stood, she greeted them with a beaming smile and reproached Zhou Rui's wife for not announcing them sooner. Granny Liu had already bowed several times from the floor and wished the young mistress good health. Xifeng hurriedly said, “Sister Zhou, help her up at once. Please don't bow anymore; do sit down. I am young and do not know all our relations well, nor do I know which generation you belong to, so I dare not presume to address you.” Zhou Rui's wife hastily replied, “This is the very granny I just told you about.” Xifeng nodded. Granny Liu was now seated on the edge of the kang. Ban'er hid behind her, and no matter how they coaxed him to come out and bow, he stubbornly refused.

p.src: Xifeng smiled. “When relatives do not visit one another often, they grow estranged. Those who know the truth will say that you have grown tired of us and will not come often; those spiteful people who do not will suppose that we look down on everyone.” Granny Liu hurriedly invoked the Buddha and said, “Our family has fallen on hard times, and we cannot afford to make visits. If we came here, we would only expose ourselves to the young mistress's ridicule; even the gentlemen who manage the household would think it unseemly.” Xifeng laughed. “What a dreadful thing to say! We merely trade on the hollow prestige of our forefathers and hold a few poorly paid official posts. Who among us possesses anything? We are nothing but the empty shell of former days. As the saying goes, ‘Even the imperial court has three branches of poor relations’; how much more must that be true of you and me?” With that, she asked Zhou Rui's wife whether she had reported the visitors to the lady of the house. Zhou Rui's wife replied, “I am waiting for your instructions, Second Mistress.” Xifeng said, “Go and see. If she has company or business, let it be; if she is free, report the matter and see what she says.” Zhou Rui's wife assented and went out.

p.src: Meanwhile, Xifeng ordered someone to fetch Ban'er some fruit. She had barely begun making small talk when a number of the household's married female stewards arrived to report on their business. When Ping'er announced them, Xifeng said, “I am entertaining guests now. Have them report again this evening. If anything is truly urgent, bring the person in and I shall deal with it at once.” Ping'er went out and returned after a while, saying, “I asked them all. There was nothing urgent, so I dismissed them.” Xifeng nodded. Presently Zhou Rui's wife returned and said to Xifeng, “Madam says that she has no leisure today, and that it will be just the same if Second Mistress keeps the visitors company. She thanks them for kindly remembering her. If they have merely come for a visit, that is all well and good; but if they have anything to say, they should tell Second Mistress freely, for it is all the same.” Granny Liu said, “There is really nothing to say. I only came to pay my respects to the elder mistress and the young mistress, as is proper between relatives.” Zhou Rui's wife said, “If there is nothing to say, then no matter. But if there is, tell Second Mistress freely; it is the same as telling Madam.” As she spoke, she kept signaling to Granny Liu with her eyes. Granny Liu understood. Before she could speak, her face flushed crimson. She wanted to remain silent, yet if she did, what had she come for today? Suppressing her shame, she had no choice but to say, “Strictly speaking, since this is the first time I have met you, young mistress, I ought not to mention it. But having come such a great distance to see you, I can hardly avoid speaking.” She had only reached this point when the young servants at the inner gate were heard announcing, “The young master from the Eastern Mansion has come in.” Xifeng hurriedly stopped Granny Liu. “You need say no more.” At the same time, she asked, “Where is Master Rong?” The sound of booted footsteps approached all the way to the room, and in came a youth of seventeen or eighteen, with delicate features and a graceful figure, clad in a light fur robe, a jeweled sash, sumptuous clothes, and a splendid cap. At that moment Granny Liu did not know whether to remain seated or stand, and there was nowhere for her to hide. Xifeng laughed. “Just stay seated. This is my nephew.” Only then did Granny Liu sit down again on the edge of the kang, fidgeting with embarrassment.

p.src: Jia Rong said with a smile, “My father sent me to ask a favor of you, Aunt. He says that tomorrow we are entertaining an important guest and would like to borrow the glass bed-screen that your aunt gave you last time. We shall display it briefly and return it at once.” “You are a day too late,” said Xifeng. “I gave it to someone yesterday.” Hearing this, Jia Rong chuckled and knelt with one knee against the edge of the kang. “If you will not lend it to me, Aunt, they will say again that I do not know how to ask properly, and I shall get another good beating. Please take pity on your poor nephew.” Xifeng laughed. “Really, you people! Is everything belonging to the Wang family necessarily finer than anything else? You have all those fine things stored away at your own place, yet you refuse to see them and insist that mine are the best.” “But none of them is as fine as this!” Jia Rong replied with a smile. “I beg you to be merciful.” “If it gets so much as a scratch,” Xifeng warned him, “you had better look to your hide!” She then ordered Ping'er to fetch the key to the storeroom upstairs and summon several trustworthy servants to carry the screen over. Jia Rong beamed with delight. “I shall take some men and fetch it myself, rather than let them knock it about.” With that, he rose and went out.

p.src: Only then did Grannie Liu recover her composure and continue, “I brought your nephew here today for no other reason than that his father and mother at home have not even enough to eat. Now that the weather has turned cold, we could think of no way out, so I had no choice but to bring your nephew and appeal to you.” Then she nudged Ban'er. “What did your father tell you at home before you came? What did he send us here to do? All you do is eat fruit!” Xifeng had understood long before. Hearing that the old woman did not know how to express herself, she stopped her with a smile. “You need say no more. I understand.” Then she asked Zhou Rui's wife, “Do you know whether this old lady has had breakfast?” Grannie Liu hastened to reply, “We set out for here at daybreak. How could we have had time to eat?” On hearing this, Xifeng promptly ordered a meal to be served. Before long Zhou Rui's wife had a guest's meal laid in the east room, then came back and took Grannie Liu and Ban'er there to eat. “Sister Zhou,” said Xifeng, “please look after them well. I cannot keep them company.” She then went into the east room. Later Xifeng called Zhou Rui's wife back and asked what she had told the mistress and what the mistress had said. Zhou Rui's wife replied, “The mistress said that their family was not originally of the same clan as ours. They merely shared the same surname, and because their ancestor once held office together with our old master, the two families happened to acknowledge kinship. There has not been much intercourse between us in recent years. Still, when they visited us in the past, we never sent them away empty-handed. Since she has come today out of goodwill to see us, we must not treat her slightingly. If she has any request, you are to use your own judgment.” “That explains it,” said Xifeng. “If we were truly one family, how could I have known nothing whatever about them?”

Xifeng smiled. “Please sit down and hear what I have to say, Grannie. I have understood what you meant just now. Between relatives, we ought properly to have helped you without waiting for you to come to our door. But household affairs are so numerous and troublesome now, and the mistress is growing older, so it is quite possible that the matter simply escaped her attention. Besides, I have only lately taken charge of some household business and know nothing about all these relatives. And though from outside our household may appear grand and flourishing, a great house has great difficulties of its own—though others would scarcely believe it if we told them. Still, you have come such a long way today, and this is the first time we have met and you have asked me for help. How could I let you return empty-handed? As it happens, the mistress gave me twenty taels of silver yesterday to make clothes for my maids, and I have not touched it yet. If you do not think it too little, take it for the present.”

p.src: When Grannie Liu first heard Xifeng speak of hardship, she assumed there would be nothing for her, and her heart began to pound. But when she then heard that she was to receive twenty taels, delight sent a tingling through her whole body. “Ah, I know very well that you have difficulties too. But as the proverb says, ‘Even a camel starved to death is bigger than a horse.’ However hard things may be for you, one hair plucked from your venerable body is thicker than our waists!” Embarrassed by her coarse speech, Zhou Rui's wife kept signaling with her eyes for her to stop. Xifeng saw this but merely smiled and took no notice. She ordered Ping'er to bring the packet of silver from the previous day and another string of cash, and place them both before Grannie Liu. Then Xifeng said, “Here are twenty taels of silver. For now, use them to make the child some winter clothes. If you refuse to take them, then you truly will be showing resentment toward me. Use this cash to hire a cart for the journey. Whenever you have leisure, come and visit us. That is how relatives should behave. It is growing late, so I shall not detain you with empty courtesies. When you get home, give my regards to all those to whom they are due.” As she spoke, she rose to her feet.

u.src: When Grannie Liu first heard Xifeng speak of hardship, she assumed there would be nothing for her, and her heart began to pound. But when she then heard that she was to receive twenty taels, delight sent a tingling through her whole body. “Ah, I know very well that you have difficulties too.
But as the proverb says, ‘Even a camel starved to death is bigger than a horse.’ However hard things may be for you, one hair plucked from your venerable body is thicker than our waists!”
Embarrassed by her coarse speech, Zhou Rui's wife kept signaling with her eyes for her to stop.
Xifeng saw this but merely smiled and took no notice. She ordered Ping'er to bring the packet of silver from the previous day and another string of cash, and place them both before Grannie Liu.
Then Xifeng said, “Here are twenty taels of silver. For now, use them to make the child some winter clothes.
If you refuse to take them, then you truly will be showing resentment toward me.
Use this cash to hire a cart for the journey.
Whenever you have leisure, come and visit us. That is how relatives should behave.
It is growing late, so I shall not detain you with empty courtesies. When you get home, give my regards to all those to whom they are due.”
As she spoke, she rose to her feet.

p.src: Grannie Liu poured out endless thanks, took the silver and cash, and followed Zhou Rui's wife outside. Zhou Rui's wife said, “Good heavens, Grannie! Why did you lose the power of speech the moment you saw her? You began at once by calling the boy ‘your nephew.’ Forgive me for speaking plainly, but even if he really were her nephew, you should have put it more tactfully. Master Rong is her proper nephew. How could another nephew suddenly appear from nowhere?” Grannie Liu laughed. “My dear sister, when I saw her, I was so overwhelmed with affection that I could do nothing but adore her. How could I possibly have found the words to speak?” Conversing as they went, the two returned to Zhou Rui's home and sat there for a while. Grannie Liu wanted to leave a piece of silver for the Zhou children to buy fruit, but Zhou Rui's wife thought nothing of such a sum and steadfastly refused it. Grannie Liu thanked her profusely and departed again by the rear gate. And so it is said:
